guide.summary: A thin membrane on one edge: dissolved things seep through slowly, nothing living crosses.
guide.biology: Dialysis membranes have pores small enough to let dissolved molecules through while holding back cells and viruses.
guide.rules: A fine membrane sits on the edge between two cells, not on a cell. Dissolved things (food, gases, nutrient, salt, acid, base, buffer, silicate, metabolite, inhibitors) and activities (enzymes, signal, RIVAL and the like) spread across it at 25 % of their ordinary rate. Viruses, organisms and deposits never cross it. Warmth passes it as it passes open water. It cannot sit on the rim of the dish. A dish holds at most 512 edge barriers, and two barriers on one edge are refused. No additional modeled reaction.
guide.example: Put a line of membranes across a sugar patch: the sugar seeps through, while the swimmers stay on their own side.
